body.statement: For \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), \[2[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n}]_+\le L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\le2(1-\alpha).\] Hence \(\tau_n\to0\) implies \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\to2(1-\alpha)\). If \(s>1\) is fixed and \(\lambda_n\) remains in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), then the same limit holds.
body.justification: This identifies an exact nonshrinking phase and removes a spurious higher-smoothness transition based only on location entropy.
body.gap: Mikusheva (2010) links weak-instrument test power to confidence-set length, while the banked parent obtained only a two-label location mixture; neither yields the full-label coefficient \(2(1-\alpha)\) in this unknown-cutoff class.
body.consumer: An analyst can recognize regimes in which any apparently narrow interval must owe its informativeness to restrictions stronger than the maintained H\"older class.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove the upper bound by displaying one data-driven honest rule.  Define
\[
 I_n^0(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=
 \begin{cases}
 \Theta,&X_1>\alpha,\\
 \varnothing,&X_1\le\alpha.
 \end{cases}
\]
Both values are connected subsets of \(\Theta\), and the rule is measurable.  By ass:uniform-running-variable, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\),
\[
 P\{\theta_P\in I_n^0\}=P(X_1>\alpha)=1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 E_P|I_n^0|=2(1-\alpha).
\]
The definition of \(L_n^\star\) therefore implies \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\le2(1-\alpha)\).

For the converse, let \(I_n\) be any rule admissible in def:minimax-length.  Proposition prop:moving-cutoff-membership-kl implies that every \(P_t\), \(t\in[-1,1]\), belongs to \(\mathcal P_n\) and has \(\theta_{P_t}=t\).  Honesty and the total-variation comparison in that proposition give, for each \(t\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_0^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
 &\ge P_t^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
      -\operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})\\
 &\ge1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}
 \ge1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Probabilities are nonnegative.  Tonelli's theorem applied to the nonnegative measurable function \(\mathbf 1\{t\in I_n\}\) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{P_0}|I_n|
 &=\int_{-1}^1P_0^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}\,dt\\
 &\ge2[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n}]_+.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(P_0\in\mathcal P_n\), taking the supremum over \(P\), and then the infimum over every honest \(I_n\), proves the asserted lower bound.

If \(\tau_n\to0\), the two bounds converge to \(2(1-\alpha)\), proving the first limit.  Now fix \(s>1\) and suppose \(\lambda_n\) remains in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\).  If \(\kappa_n\) failed to converge to zero, some subsequence would have \(\kappa_n\ge\epsilon>0\); on that subsequence
\[
 \lambda_n=\frac{n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}}{\log(e/\kappa_n)}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
contrary to compactness.  Thus \(\kappa_n\to0\).  The defining identity for \(\lambda_n\) can be rearranged as
\[
 \tau_n=\lambda_n\kappa_n^{1-1/s}\log(e/\kappa_n).
\]
Because \(1-1/s>0\), the last two factors tend to zero while \(\lambda_n\) is bounded.  Hence \(\tau_n\to0\), and the already proved sandwich gives the same limit.
